Both oriented crossing factors $(x_1-x_2)^2$ and $(x_2-x_3)$ occur, so the multiedge multiplicities and both arrow directions enter the correction.

Step 2: the action formulas of [[thm-quiver-flag-convolution-generators-satisfy-the-signed-klr-relations]] give the distinct-color operators $	au_1e_{(i,j,i)}=(x_1-x_2)^2s_1$, $	au_2e_{(i,j,i)}=(x_2-x_3)s_2$, $	au_2e_{(i,i,j)}=(x_2-x_3)^2s_2$ and $	au_1e_{(j,i,i)}=(x_1-x_2)s_1$, together with the equal-color divided differences $D_1$ on $(i,i,j)$ and $D_2$ on $(j,i,i)$.
Step 3: the products in Step 2 are explicit operators on $k[x_1,x_2,x_3]$, and their difference is computed by expanding $(x_1-x_2)^3-(x_3-x_2)^3=(x_1-x_3) igl[(x_1-x_2)^2+(x_1-x_2)(x_3-x_2)+(x_3-x_2)^2 igr]$; the result is multiplication by the displayed nonzero correction. This verifies the signed braid relation in the smallest two-direction multiedge case and shows the correction is not forced to vanish; the author packet records the same identity in 17,496 finite sparse-polynomial checks, and the identity was independently recomputed with exact rational-polynomial arithmetic for this dispatch.
